children: S&P 500, NASDAQ EDGE TENTATIVELY HIGHER WHILE SMALL CAPS TAKE COMFORTABLE LEAD
Wall Street on Tuesday struggled to extend Monday's robust rally, in which investors rediscovered their enthusiasm for all things AI and pushed the Nasdaq
to a record closing high.
The S&P 500
could follow suit today. The bellwether index, currently barely green, is hovering just below its all-time closing high reached just over a month ago.
The Dow
turned pale red after the first few minutes of trading. The small-cap Russell 2000
is enjoying a sizeable lead over its larger-cap counterparts.
On the sector level, communication services
is enjoying a comfortable lead among the S&P 500's 11 major groups, with energy
and financials
vying for last place.
Elsewhere, recently beaten-up sectors are finding some favor. Housing market-related stocks (.SPCOMHOME),
, airlines (.SPCOMAIR), and travel/leisure shares (.SPCOMHOTL) are outperformers.

Washington and Tehran dropped hints that they could shortly resume negotiations to end their conflict. As a result, crude prices dropped and Treasury yields eased, reflecting some optimism that war-related price pressures could begin to ebb sooner rather than later.

U.S. Federal Reserve appearances today include New York Fed President John Williams, Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin, with Q&A expected after Barkin's remarks. Their words will likely be dissected for clues regarding the duration and extent of the current tightening phase aimed at taming war-related inflation.
Here's where things stood as of 10:03 a.m. EDT:
S&P 500, Nasdaq modestly green; Dow flips red
Comm Svcs leads S&P 500 sector gainers; financials are weakest group
Euro STOXX 600 index up ~0.4%
Dollar edges higher; gold slips; bitcoin down; US crude pares losses
US 10-year Treasury yield edges down to ~4.95%
